To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynamic reactivity of single cortical neurons to the isolated action of Glu and Ach is different.

the probability, the direction, and the magnitude of changes of neuronal activity in response to repeated isolated action of the transmitters were different in the course of Glu- and ACh-induced responses.
the probability, direction, and magnitude of the mean neuronal firing rate changes are different for Glu and ACH.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamic reactivity of single neurons to the repeated application of L-glutamic acid (Glu) and ACh in unanesthetised rats.
the analysis of the probability of changes of mean firing rates of cortical neurons in response to the repeated action of the transmitters Glu and ACH.
the dynamics of the responses of cortical neurons to repeated isolated applications of L-glutamic acid and acetylcholin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Glu-induced activity is more sensitive than that induced by ACh to the changes of the neuronal background activity, and that Glu and ACl exert their functional effects in different ways.
Glu has a higher probability of inducing changes in the neuronal activity, but ACh has the higher probability of inducing the more profound and more specific changes.
the Glu-induced activity is more labile than that of ACh.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of the neuronal responses to Glu and ACl is different.
Glu is a more powerful and specific modulator of neuronal excitability than ACh.
Glu and ACl have different roles in the dynamics of cortical neuron firing during learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Glu is a more dynamic neurotransmitter than ACh.

the probability of changes of the background and transmitter-induced neuronal activity in response to the repeated applications of the same transmitter is higher than in response to the applications of the other transmitter, but the magnitude of these changes may be different for the different transmitters.
the dynamic reactivity of the neurons to Glu is more pronounced in comparison with the dynamic reactivity to ACh.
